finding.claim: Unvalidated iconUrl supplied via PUT /profile is fetched server-side with GET by the nightly sync() job, enabling blind SSRF to arbitrary http/https hosts reachable from the server.
finding.source: icon parameter of update(String webhook, String icon) (Profile.java:11), per the PUT /profile comment on line 10; the HTTP handler is not in this repo.
finding.sink: c.send(HttpRequest GET to URI.create(iconUrl), BodyHandlers.ofByteArray()) in sync() (Profile.java:23-24).

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon; stored with no validation
sync() calls URI.create(iconUrl) with no check
HttpClient.send issues GET from server; response body discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: Lines 12-14 validate only webhook, not icon. No scheme allowlist beyond HttpRequest's http/https restriction (file:/ftp: rejected at build time). No host allowlist, no private/link-local IP block, no connect-time address pinning. Redirect policy of injected client c not visible; default is NEVER. Response body is discarded, so the attacker gets no direct read-back.

verdict.guard_found: none in src/Profile.java: update() validates only webhook (Profile.java:12-14), and icon is stored unchecked at Profile.java:16 and passed to URI.create at Profile.java:23 with no host, scheme, or IP check. The PUT /profile handler that would supply icon is not in this directory, so any validation there is unknown.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (Profile.java:11, 16, 23-24), and no guard exists on the icon path in this file, but the claimed source is only a comment ("PUT /profile", Profile.java:10). The HTTP handler that would show whether icon is attacker-supplied, and whether it is authenticated or validated, is not in the repo, so the source and any handler-side guard cannot be decided from the code available.
